subject: physics
question_text: A body slides down a rough inclined plane of inclination θ. Derive an expression for its acceleration.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The forces
lines: Three forces act on the body: its weight
m g vertically down, the normal force N
perpendicular to the surface, and friction f
up the slope, opposing the sliding.
steps.why: Friction always opposes the relative sliding, so for a body moving DOWN the slope it must point UP the slope.
common_mistakes: Drawing friction down the slope, which would speed the body up instead of slowing it.

recall.must_convey: That weight acts down, the normal force acts perpendicular to the surface, and friction acts up the slope.

steps.memory_tip: Count three: weight, normal force, friction. There is no fourth force pushing it down the slope.
steps.margin_note: First mark. All three forces named with their directions. Friction points up the slope.

steps.label: Resolving them
lines: Resolve the weight along and perpendicular
to the plane. Perpendicular to the plane the

lines.text: N = m g cos θ,   f = μ N = μ m g cos θ

lines: Along the plane, the net force gives ma:

lines.text: m a = m g sin θ − μ m g cos θ

steps.why: Resolving ALONG and PERPENDICULAR to the plane, rather than horizontally and vertically, is what keeps the acceleration in one equation.
common_mistakes: Using N = mg on an incline; the normal force is only mg cos θ.

recall.must_convey: That N is mg cos theta, friction is mu mg cos theta, and ma is mg sin theta minus mu mg cos theta.
accept: ma equals mg sin theta minus mu mg cos theta

steps.memory_tip: Test with θ = 0: cos 0 = 1 gives N = mg, and sin 0 = 0 gives nothing along the plane.
steps.margin_note: Second and third marks. One for N = mg cos θ, one for the equation along the plane.

steps.label: The result

lines.text: a = g (sin θ − μ cos θ)

lines: If tan θ ≤ μ the bracket is not positive and
the body does not slide at all.
steps.why: The mass cancels, so a heavy body and a light body slide down the same slope with the same acceleration. The no-slide check tan θ ≤ μ uses the static coefficient μ_s, for a body placed at rest. A body already sliding with tan θ < μ_k slows down and stops; negative a means deceleration.
common_mistakes: Keeping m in the final answer after it has cancelled.

recall.must_convey: That a equals g into sin theta minus mu cos theta, and the body does not slide if tan theta is at most mu.
accept: g into sin theta minus mu cos theta
does not slide if tan theta is less than mu
heard_as: sin theta minus mu cos theta

steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Cancel m and box the result. The no-slide line is one extra sentence.

insider_note: Resolving carries 2 of the 4 marks and depends on N = m g cos θ, not m g. The force diagram is the first mark, before any algebra.
